correctness.rationale: A homomorphism sends the odd-order rotation subgroup into itself. If the reflection generator maps to 1, inversion forces twice its additive restriction to vanish, hence that restriction is zero. Otherwise the reflection image is us, and idempotence is exactly P²=P with P(u)=0. The composition law agrees with affine composition. The product of commuting affine idempotents fixes its nonempty image pointwise under every factor, so for a fixed tuple of linear projections the translations comprise the image of x↦((1−P_i)x)_i and have the claimed quotient cardinality. Boolean joint projections give direct decompositions with the all-one summand equal to the common linear image. Each labeled type is one automorphism orbit with blockwise stabilizer. The automorphism order uses the product of sizes of all Hom blocks and the invertible fraction for diagonal equal-exponent blocks: reduction modulo p is block triangular by exponent, and invertibility there implies invertibility on the finite p-group. The tuple and clique counts follow by adding the universal trivial map and partitioning tuple positions by repeated entry (signed Stirling inversion). Refining joint decompositions into cyclic prime-power factors yields maximal cliques. The constant map pins down the chosen fixed point and the atoms of the full projection family recover the unordered summands, giving the claimed stabilizer and count. The empty tuple has the sole all-one word and weight 1. For unequal p-exponents the embedding factor is p^{2a}; assigning the two factors to equal/different words gives the stated formula, with positive p^b coefficient for t≥1, versus no dependence on b in the unweighted count. Independent enumeration reproduces (1,136,1864,11152), 137 total maps, 2137 full ordered commuting pairs, and 243 maximal cliques of size 5.
residual_risks: The example is finite corroboration, not the justification for arbitrary odd finite abelian kernels. No even-kernel classification or reconstruction for all kernels is shown.

It varies with the previously invisible large cyclic exponent and therefore gives a concrete, precisely scoped distinction between additive and generalized-dihedral retraction statistics. The general census determines the whole clique polynomial and maximal-family sizes/counts, including mixed-prime and mixed-exponent types, not a numerical instance alone.
